# MarketForge LinkedIn Organic

Apply V3 §3.4 (LinkedIn organic) + `ai-saturation-watch.md` Cycle 3.

## Global quality rules

- Company pages have been deprioritized for ~3 years. Don't rely on them.
- Founder + 2-3 employee accounts > company page.
- Carousels + text-only posts > link posts (LinkedIn down-ranks outbound links).
- 1 post/day for founders; 2-3/week for employees.
- Reply-to-every-comment in first 90 minutes (Justin Welsh signature mechanic).
- AI-written LinkedIn content is saturated; founder voice survives.
- Selection-bias caveat: for every Welsh-style outlier there are 10K creators who posted daily for 18 months and grew to 2K followers.

## Purpose

1. Account strategy (founder + 2-3 employee identification).
2. Voice + persona per account.
3. Post cadence + format hierarchy.
4. Hook formulas (PAIPS + alternatives).
5. Reply discipline (90-min response window).
6. DM-based selling (NOT "book a demo" CTAs).
7. Repurposing pipeline (LinkedIn → X → newsletter).

## Inputs
- `brand-strategy.md`, `messaging-architecture.md`, `narrative-and-story.md`, `voice-of-customer.md`, `icp-and-personas/`.

## Outputs
- `docs/marketing-plan/07-organic-social/linkedin-organic.md`
- DEC-410 to DEC-419

## Structure

```markdown
# LinkedIn Organic Strategy

## Account strategy

### Primary: Founder
- Cadence: 1 post/day (5/week minimum; weekends optional).
- Voice: Founder's own.
- Topic mix: 40% category POV / 30% behind-the-scenes / 20% customer stories / 10% personal.

### Supporting: 2-3 employees
- Cadence: 2-3 posts/week each.
- Voice: Their own — NOT founder ghost-written.
- Topic mix: Tied to their expertise area.

### Company page (deprioritized)
- Post 2-3x/week but expect low reach.
- Use for: hiring posts, press releases, customer announcements, brand-voice content.
- Do NOT invest founder time here.

## Content format hierarchy

### Tier 1 (highest reach)
- Text-only posts (no link).
- Carousel posts (PDF / image carousel up to 10 slides).
- Video posts (native upload, NOT YouTube link).

### Tier 2
- Image + text.
- Polls.

### Tier 3 (downranked)
- Link posts (post link in body or comment).

### Tier 4 (rarely used)
- Articles (long-form on LinkedIn directly) — fine for SEO-style content but most reach is in text/carousels.

## Hook formulas

### PAIPS (attributed to Justin Welsh)
- Pain → Agitation → Insight → Proof → Solution

### Alternatives
- **Story hook:** "Three years ago I was [bad state]. Last month I [good outcome]. Here's what I changed."
- **Contrarian hook:** "Everyone says [common belief]. After running [N experiments], I'm convinced [opposite]."
- **Specific number hook:** "We just hit [specific number]. Three things made the difference."
- **Behind-the-scenes hook:** "We just shipped [feature]. The 47 interviews that led to it taught me [specific thing]."
- **Failure hook:** "I shut down a channel that was driving 40% of pipeline. Here's the test that proved it was incremental fraud."

## Post structure

### Hook (first 1-2 lines)
- Stops the scroll.
- Must work as a preview without expansion.

### Body
- One specific argument.
- 100-300 words typical.
- Short paragraphs (1-3 sentences each).
- Line breaks for visual rhythm.

### Sign-off / CTA
- Soft engagement ask ("What's your take?").
- Or substantive ("This becomes a longer piece in my newsletter — link in profile if interested").
- NOT "book a demo" (kills reach).

## Reply discipline

- First 90 minutes after posting: reply to every comment.
- Engagement begets reach. Algorithm rewards comment density.
- DM thoughtful comment-engagers within 24 hours (not pitch — relationship).

## Repurposing pipeline

1. LinkedIn original post.
2. Same content → X thread (24h later).
3. Same content → newsletter (week-later).
4. Same content → blog (if expanded with original data).
5. Top performers → ad creative (Thought Leader Ads).

## DM-based selling

- "Book a demo" CTAs underperform.
- Instead: build relationship → DM offer of value → meeting from inbound DM.
- Use the comment-then-DM pattern (engage on their content, build context, then DM).

## Voice discipline

NOT acceptable:
- Three-word triplets ("Bold. Beautiful. Built.").
- Em-dash overuse.
- "Not just X — Y" without follow-through.
- Generic "here's what I learned" without specifics.
- AI cadence patterns (see `anti-slop-marketing-rubric.md`).

YES:
- Specific numbers, named people, named companies.
- One-line statements that are unhedged.
- Stories with timestamps.
- Verbatim quotes from customers.

## Cadence enforcement

### Daily (founder)
- Morning: post (8-10am local in target audience timezone).
- 30-min calendar block for engagement (replies, comments on others' posts).
- Mid-day check (top 3 of own posts; reply if traction).

### Weekly
- Monday: post planning session (themes for the week).
- Friday: review what worked; capture for repurposing.

### Monthly
- Audit: top posts, engagement rate, follower growth, DM-driven inbound.

## KPIs

Primary:
- DM-driven meetings booked.
- Newsletter subscriber growth (if linked).
- Sales pipeline attributed to LinkedIn (self-report survey).

Secondary:
- Follower growth.
- Engagement rate.
- Comment density on posts.

NOT primary:
- Follower count alone.
- Impression count.

## Decision cards
[DEC-410 to DEC-419]

## Kill criteria
- 6-12 months; follower growth flat + engagement <1% + no DM-based inbound + no brand-search lift → re-evaluate voice / topic mix / commitment level.

## What we are intentionally NOT doing
- AI-ghostwritten LinkedIn content (saturation).
- Posting from company page as primary (deprioritized).
- "Book a demo" CTAs in feed posts (kills reach).
- Outbound link posts (downranked).
- Buying followers / engagement.

## Sources and basis
V3 §3.4.
```
